What I want next. A senior or staff backend engineer role, ideally on payments or ledger infrastructure. Money movement, ledgers, reconciliation, payouts, the systems where being wrong by a cent actually matters and somebody in finance notices. That's where I've been happiest and honestly where I'm best. I'd also be happy in platform engineering, the internal platform stuff, pulling services out of a monolith, reliability, on-call that doesn't burn people out, the kind of thing I did at Shiftwell. As long as it's backend and systems.

Companies that excite me: places where payments are core to the product, not a side feature. Brickyard Pay, Cartwheel Commerce, Saltbox, that kind of company. Developer infrastructure like Edgewarden too, I really enjoyed building tollgate and I'd love to work on that kind of problem at real scale. Mid-size to large is fine. I'm not looking for a ten-person seed startup right now, I need some stability after the last couple of years. I want a team that writes design docs, does real blameless postmortems, and has a sane on-call rotation.

What I want to avoid. No defense work, no government cleared work. I did five years of it at Redstone and I'm done with it. No frontend roles. I can read React, I can fix a button, but it's not what I do and I'd be mediocre at it. And not engineering management right now. I've been asked before, and maybe in two or three years once I'm back in the rhythm I'd look at it, but right now I want to be an individual contributor, hands on, writing code and design docs. Also not crypto. I've looked at it a few times, it's not for me.

The hard limits, so nobody wastes anybody's time:

Pay: I need at least $185,000 base. Equity is nice, but the base has to be 185 or more.

Location: I live in Atlanta and I'm staying here. My dad's here. So remote in the US, or hybrid if the office is in the Atlanta area. I won't relocate, not for any amount of money.

Travel: under 10%. An offsite or two a year is fine, a conference now and then is fine. Not weeks on the road. I did that in New Mexico motels, never again.

Clearance: I don't have an active clearance and I'm not getting one, so anything that requires an active security clearance is out, even if it's in Atlanta and pays well.

For the record, I'm a US citizen, born in Atlanta, so I don't need any visa sponsorship.

About the gap: I took about two and a half years off to care for my dad after his stroke. I'd like that explained plainly on a resume, not hidden or dressed up. I kept building things the whole time, pgledger and tollgate and the Lumenrent contract, and I'm ready to go back full time now.
